scale.name: Not bootable
scale.meaning: A clean checkout can't install, build and pass its tests.

scale.name: Bootable
scale.meaning: A clean checkout installs, builds and passes every test.

scale.name: Verifiable
scale.meaning: Agents can check their own work: the commands pass, the tests catch planted faults, the instructions are accurate and normal work needs no production access.

scale.name: Delegable
scale.meaning: Agent PRs meet the outcome targets your team set.

scale.name: Scalable
scale.meaning: Those targets held while agent PR volume at least doubled.

checks.title: Components and where changes land
checks.why: Levels follow the work, so the audit finds each package and its share of recent changes.

checks.title: Agent assets in the repo
checks.why: Shows what agent setup already exists and who maintains it. Not scored.

checks.title: Setup works from a clean checkout
checks.why: Every agent starts from a clean checkout, so setup that only works on a prepared machine breaks every agent run.

sources.claim: In the BootstrapAgent study, a reusable, verified setup cut later agents' token use by 25.9% and build time by 22.3%.
sources.caveat: Measured on the study's benchmark repositories.

checks.title: Build, lint, type-check and test commands pass
checks.why: Agents need one known way to check their own work.

checks.title: Tests catch planted faults
checks.why: Green tests aren't proof that a change is right.

sources.claim: OpenAI estimated about 30% of SWE-Bench Pro's 731 public tasks were broken, including low-coverage tests that let incomplete fixes pass.
sources.caveat: An audit of one benchmark, not of customer repositories.

checks.title: Agent instructions are accurate
checks.why: Agents follow AGENTS.md, rules and skills literally, so a stale command costs more than a missing one. No outcome study yet measures how much these files help.

checks.title: Normal work needs no production access
checks.why: Agents run with whatever access setup gives them, so normal work must never need production credentials.

clean.install.label: installs from the lockfile in a clean container

clean.test.label: passes every test in a clean container

commands.label: build, lint, type-check and test commands pass

safety.label: normal work needs no production access

lockfile.label: a frozen install reproduces the lockfile

repoLevel.rule: the lowest level among active components, the assessed components with at least 10% of changes over 90 days; a component joins or leaves that set only after two audits on the same side of the line, and components the audit can't assess never set it

mutation.targeting: files imported by the component's tests, most recently changed first

owner.title: Name an owner for agent readiness
owner.decision: Who owns agent readiness for this repo
owner.why: Someone has to approve setup changes, set outcome targets and watch the weekly recheck.
owner.doneWhen: An owner is recorded with `readiness roadmap owner`.

steps.title: Pick an owner
steps.detail: A person or team who approves setup changes and sets outcome targets.

steps.title: Record it
steps.detail: `readiness roadmap owner "<team or role>"` stores it in `.agent-readiness/roadmap.json`.

clean.install.title: Make {component} install from the lockfile in a clean container
clean.install.why: In a clean container, the frozen install for {component} fails: {diagnosis}.

steps.title: Reproduce it
steps.detail: Run `readiness replay --component {component}` and read the install output in the evidence log.

steps.title: Fix the install
steps.detail: Commit the lockfile, declare missing system packages in the setup script, or pass registry variables with `--registry-env`.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness replay --component {component}`.

clean.build.title: Make {component} build in a clean container
clean.build.why: In a clean container, the build for {component} fails: {diagnosis}.

steps.title: Reproduce it
steps.detail: Run `readiness replay --component {component}` and read the build output.

steps.title: Fix the build
steps.detail: Usually a missing generated file, tool or environment variable that a prepared machine already has.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness replay --component {component}`.

clean.test:service.title: Set up {service} for agents in {component}
clean.test:service.size: Small: setup scripts and environment config, no source changes
clean.test:service.why: In a clean container, {component}'s tests fail because nothing starts {service}: {diagnosis}.

steps.title: Ask the agent to fix it
steps.detail: Say "fix the primary blocker". It drafts install and start scripts and a `.cursor/environment.json` with `readiness draft-env`.

steps.title: The agent proves it
steps.detail: `readiness replay --component {component}` must pass every test before the fix is offered.

steps.title: Review and merge
steps.detail: Check that the start script only starts local services and names no production URLs.

steps.title: Point Cloud Agents at it
steps.detail: A team admin sets the Cloud Agent environment to read `.cursor/environment.json`; committing the file alone changes no environment.

steps.title: Re-audit
steps.detail: The next audit confirms Level 1 and can now plant faults in {component}.

clean.test:credential.title: Remove the production credential from {component}'s tests
clean.test:credential.decision: Which fake or sandbox value tests should use
clean.test:credential.why: {component}'s tests fail without a production credential: {diagnosis}.
clean.test:credential.doneWhen: `readiness replay --component {component}` passes every test with no credentials provided.

steps.title: Find the read
steps.detail: Look for the environment variable named in the test failure.

steps.title: Use a test double
steps.detail: Fake the client in tests, or read a sandbox value from a checked-in test config.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness replay --component {component}` with no credentials set.

clean.test:missing.title: Add tests and a test command to {component}
clean.test:missing.size: Medium: a test runner and first tests in {component}
clean.test:missing.decision: Which behavior the first tests should pin down
clean.test:missing.why: {component} has no test command, so neither agents nor reviewers can check a change automatically.
clean.test:missing.doneWhen: `readiness replay --component {component}` runs the new tests and they pass.

steps.title: Pick a runner the repo can install
steps.detail: For example `node --test`, Vitest or pytest, added as the `test` script.

steps.title: Test the most changed code first
steps.detail: Assert results and edge cases for the files that change most often.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Run a new audit. It runs the tests in a clean container and plants faults they should catch.

clean.test.title: Make {component}'s tests pass from a clean checkout
clean.test.why: In a clean container, {component}'s tests fail: {diagnosis}.

steps.title: Reproduce it
steps.detail: Run `readiness replay --component {component}` and read the failing test output.

steps.title: Fix what a prepared machine was hiding
steps.detail: Usually a missing service, tool, fixture file or environment variable.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness replay --component {component}`.

commands.title: Fix the failing {kinds} command in {component}
commands.why: The {kinds} command for {component} fails at HEAD: {diagnosis}.

steps.title: Reproduce it
steps.detail: Run `readiness run --component {component}` and read the failing command's output.

steps.title: Fix it at HEAD
steps.detail: Agents rely on these commands to check their own work, so they must pass on a clean main branch.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness run --component {component}`.

faults.title: Make {component}'s tests catch wrong behavior
faults.decision: What the untested behavior in {files} should be
faults.why: The audit planted {planted} faults in {component} in a throwaway copy, and the tests caught {caught}.
faults.doneWhen: A new audit's fresh planted faults in {component} are all caught.

steps.title: Decide the intended behavior
steps.detail: For the files named here, write down what correct behavior is, including edge cases.

steps.title: Write tests that pin it down
steps.detail: Assert results and edge cases, not just that code runs.

steps.title: Prove it with fresh faults
steps.detail: Run a new audit. It plants different faults than this one, so tests aimed at one audit's faults don't help.

steps.title: Review
steps.detail: `readiness diff` flags any deleted test or new skip marker, so nothing was weakened to pass.

instructions.title: Fix the stale agent instructions
instructions.why: {failedCount} instructions agents would follow are wrong: {diagnosis}.

steps.title: Fix each listed item
steps.detail: {itemList}

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: `readiness run --instructions` replays every command and checks every path.

safety:secret.title: Remove committed secrets
safety:secret.size: Small: {fileCount} files, plus rotating the secrets
safety:secret.why: The repo contains {count} committed secrets ({types}); agents and their logs can read them.

steps.title: Rotate first
steps.detail: Treat every listed secret as exposed and rotate it before removing it.

steps.title: Remove and ignore
steps.detail: Move values to the secret store and add the files to `.gitignore`.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness scan`.

safety:hook.title: Remove the network-piped install hook
safety:hook.decision: Whether the hook's script can be vendored and reviewed
safety:hook.why: An install hook downloads and runs a script ({detail}); every agent install would run it unreviewed.

steps.title: Vendor or delete the script
steps.detail: Commit the script it downloads, reviewed, or remove the hook.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness scan`.

safety:credential.title: Stop normal work from needing production credentials
safety:credential.decision: Which sandbox credentials agents may use
safety:credential.why: Normal build or test commands read production credentials ({detail}).
safety:credential.doneWhen: `readiness scan` reports no production credential reads in normal work.

steps.title: Replace with sandbox values
steps.detail: Tests and builds use fakes or sandbox accounts.

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness scan` and `readiness replay`.

toolchain.title: Pin the toolchain versions
toolchain.size: Small: one or two version files
toolchain.why: The repo doesn't pin {missing}, so agents and CI can build with different versions.

steps.title: Add the pins
steps.detail: {advice}

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness scan` and `readiness replay`.

lockfile.title: Make the install reproducible from a lockfile
lockfile.why: A frozen install doesn't reproduce exact dependencies: {diagnosis}.
lockfile.doneWhen: `readiness replay` reports a frozen install with the lockfile unchanged.

steps.title: Commit a lockfile
steps.detail: {advice}

steps.title: Prove it
steps.detail: Rerun `readiness replay`.

delegate.title: Give agents work in {component}
delegate.decision: Which tasks go to agents first, and who reviews them
delegate.why: {component} is already at Level 2, so agents can check their own work there.
delegate.doneWhen: Agent PRs in {component} appear in the outcome numbers.

steps.title: Pick 3 to 5 real tasks
steps.detail: Well-scoped tasks that touch only {component}.

steps.title: Hand them to agents
steps.detail: Agents run the verify skill before they push.

steps.title: Review as usual
steps.detail: The next audit counts these PRs by component.

targets.title: Set your Level 3 targets
targets.decision: The merge rate, first-time CI pass rate and review load that mean agents handle work here
targets.why: Level 3 is measured against targets your team sets, and none are recorded yet.
targets.doneWhen: Targets are recorded with `readiness roadmap targets`.

steps.title: Agree the measures
steps.detail: Merge rate, first-time CI pass rate and reviewer change requests, over at least 20 agent PRs.

steps.title: Record them
steps.detail: `readiness roadmap targets --merge-rate 0.7 --first-pass 0.6 --max-changes-requested 0.3`.

steps.title: Read the next report
steps.detail: It shows the distance to each target.
